title: Console landmark tiles & vertical switcher — contextual IA prototype
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: The current Console navigation mixes workspace switching, model routes, and operational surfaces (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) in ways that increase cognitive load for users managing multiple projects and deployments. Goals: 1) Surface primary operational entry points (Dashboards, Rollouts, Costs, Models, Deployments) as ‘landmarks’ for fast orientation; 2) Keep workspace switching lightweight and discoverable, with a compact vertical switcher that expands contextually; 3) Reduce route churn and preserve state for in-flight operations (open rollout forms, active trace views); 4) Support progressive disclosure for enterprise users (role-aware links) and mobile/responsive constraints. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype for desktop + tablet breakpoints, interaction spec for routing and state preservation, accessibility checklist, microcopy set for switcher and landmark tiles, experimental A/B plan for rollout of the new IA.
acceptance_criteria: A desktop prototype exists that shows: landmark tile strip, compact vertical workspace switcher, and three example operational routes (Dashboards, Rollouts, Costs) with preserved query params when navigating between workspaces.
Prototype includes keyboard navigation for the switcher (Cmd/Ctrl+K opens, arrow keys move, Enter selects) and a clear accessible label announced by screen readers.
Design spec documents how route fallbacks behave when a user’s pinned model is unavailable and lists expected UX for automatic model variant fallback.

Usability testing with 6 participants (mix of platform engineers and product PMs) yields >= 80% success on primary tasks (find cost breakdown, start a canary rollout, switch workspace while preserving open dashboard panels).
Hand-off artifacts (Figma, interaction spec, annotated CSS tokens, a single-line PRD link) are posted and linked in this ticket.
Eng feedback recorded and a low-risk phased rollout plan is agreed (feature flag & telemetry events defined).
decisions: Use horizontal 'landmark tiles' below the topbar for primary operational surfaces to minimize left-rail depth and improve first-click discovery.

Switch workspace control becomes a compact vertical rail item (avatar + chevron) that expands to show recent workspaces and a 'Go to project' search field; pinned workspaces are shown at top of expanded rail.
Primary left rail will remain (Models, Deployments, Logs) but reduce to icons-only in compact mode; landmark tiles provide readable labels for primary operations.
Routing: preserve query params and open panel state when switching workspaces; if target workspace lacks resource, show contextual fallback banner with quick actions.
First rollout will ship behind a feature flag with telemetry for entry click rates, workspace-switch latency, and task success funnels.
Accessibility: landmarks will have ARIA roles and a visually hidden heading for screen readers; keyboard shortcuts are prioritized over deep nested focus flows.
tradeoffs: Pros: Faster discovery for key operational surfaces and fewer top-level left-rail items; Cons: horizontal landmark strip uses vertical space and may push content down on small viewports.
Keeping the left rail for secondary functions preserves muscle memory for long-time users but prolongs migration to a simpler IA.
Preserving full query state across workspace switches increases engineering complexity and requires guardrails for stale resource references.
Feature-flag rollout slows universal adoption but reduces blast radius for enterprise customers.
